### Health Analytics with R · Module 06: Causal Inference in Health Research
***
**Learning objectives**
- Conduct E-value analysis for unmeasured confounding
- Implement Rosenbaum bounds for observational studies
- Perform propensity score trimming and overlap assessment
- Build a comprehensive causal inference reporting template
- Apply placebo tests and refutation checks
- Communicate uncertainty from multiple sensitivity analyses

**Estimated time:** 2.5 hours | **Level:** Advanced | **Libraries:** `EValue`, `sensemakr`, `stats`, `ggplot2`

## 1. Setup & Dataset


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)
library(EValue)
library(sensemakr)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

mod06_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod06")
dir.create(mod06_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

logistic <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

set.seed(42)
N <- 5000
age <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 60, 12), 30), 90)
smoking <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(-1 + 0.02 * (age - 60)))
chd_history <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(-2 + 0.03 * (age - 60)))
ldl_baseline <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 140 + 20 * smoking, 30), 60), 280)
ses_score <- rnorm(N, 0, 1)
statin_logit <- -2.0 + 0.025 * (ldl_baseline - 140) + 1.0 * chd_history +
  0.02 * (age - 60) - 0.3 * ses_score
statin <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(statin_logit))
TRUE_EFFECT <- -0.8
mi_logit <- -3.0 + TRUE_EFFECT * statin + 0.03 * (age - 60) + 0.5 * smoking +
  0.8 * chd_history + 0.005 * (ldl_baseline - 140)
mi <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(mi_logit))
df <- tibble(
  age          = age,
  smoking      = smoking,
  chd_history  = chd_history,
  ldl_baseline = ldl_baseline,
  ses_score    = ses_score,
  statin       = statin,
  mi           = mi
)
COVARIATES <- c("age", "smoking", "chd_history", "ldl_baseline", "ses_score")
cat(sprintf("N=%d | Statin=%.1f%% | MI=%.1f%%\n",
            N, mean(statin) * 100, mean(mi) * 100))
```

## 2. E-Value — Unmeasured Confounding Sensitivity

The **E-value** (VanderWeele & Ding, 2017) answers:

> "How strong would an unmeasured confounder have to be (in terms of its association with both treatment and outcome) to fully explain away the observed effect?"

A large E-value means the result is robust to unmeasured confounding.

**Formula for OR:**
```
E-value = OR + sqrt(OR * (OR - 1))     if OR >= 1
E-value = 1/OR + sqrt(1/OR * (1/OR - 1))  if OR < 1
```


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Fit adjusted model
model_adj <- glm(
  mi ~ statin + age + smoking + chd_history + ldl_baseline + ses_score,
  data = df, family = binomial()
)
tid_statin <- broom::tidy(model_adj, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) |>
  filter(term == "statin")
adj_or   <- tid_statin$estimate
adj_or_lo <- tid_statin$conf.low
adj_or_hi <- tid_statin$conf.high

evalue_or <- function(OR) {
  if (OR >= 1) {
    OR + sqrt(OR * (OR - 1))
  } else {
    inv <- 1 / OR
    inv + sqrt(inv * (inv - 1))
  }
}

cat(sprintf("Adjusted OR for statin: %.3f\n", adj_or))
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# E-values across a range of OR estimates (sensitivity plot)
ors_range <- seq(0.3, 0.95, length.out = 50)
evalues_v <- vapply(ors_range, evalue_or, numeric(1))
ev_curve <- tibble(or = ors_range, evalue = evalues_v)

p_ev <- ggplot(ev_curve, aes(or, evalue)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 1, ymax = evalue), fill = "#DC2626", alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(colour = "#DC2626", linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = adj_or, colour = "#2563EB", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = ev, colour = "#2563EB", linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(
    x = "Odds Ratio (point estimate)",
    y = "E-value",
    title = "E-value Sensitivity Curve"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = adj_or, y = max(evalues_v) * 0.9,
           label = sprintf("Our estimate (OR=%.3f)\nE-value=%.2f", adj_or, ev),
           colour = "#2563EB", hjust = -0.05, size = 3)

# Contour plot: what combinations of confounder-treatment and confounder-outcome RRs explain the effect
rr_range <- seq(1, 5, length.out = 100)
grid_u <- expand.grid(rr_treat = rr_range, rr_out = rr_range)
grid_u$explained_or <- (grid_u$rr_treat * grid_u$rr_out) /
  (grid_u$rr_treat + grid_u$rr_out - 1)

p_contour <- ggplot(grid_u, aes(rr_treat, rr_out, fill = explained_or)) +
  geom_raster(interpolate = TRUE) +
  geom_contour(aes(z = explained_or), breaks = adj_or,
               colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdYlBu", name = "OR attributable to U") +
  labs(
    x = "RR(U, Treatment)",
    y = "RR(U, Outcome)",
    title = sprintf("Unmeasured confounder contour\n(black = combos that explain away OR=%.3f)", adj_or)
  )

p_evalue <- p_ev + p_contour
print(p_evalue)
```

## 3. Overlap & Positivity Assessment


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Estimate PS
ps_model <- glm(
  as.formula(paste("statin ~", paste(COVARIATES, collapse = " + "))),
  data = df, family = binomial()
)
df$ps <- predict(ps_model, type = "response")

ps_min_treated <- min(df$ps[df$statin == 1])
ps_max_control <- max(df$ps[df$statin == 0])
in_support  <- df$ps >= ps_min_treated & df$ps <= ps_max_control
pct_support <- mean(in_support) * 100

p_ps <- ggplot(df, aes(ps, fill = factor(statin))) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 40, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = ps_min_treated, xmax = ps_max_control,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#16A34A", alpha = 0.10) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("0" = "#2563EB", "1" = "#DC2626"),
    labels = c("Control", "Treated"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Propensity score",
    y = "Density",
    title = sprintf("PS Distribution: Overlap Check (common support %.0f%%)", pct_support)
  )

# IPTW weight distribution
df$w_ate <- ifelse(
  df$statin == 1,
  1 / pmin(pmax(df$ps, 0.05), 0.95),
  1 / (1 - pmin(pmax(df$ps, 0.05), 0.95))
)

p_w <- ggplot(df, aes(w_ate, fill = factor(statin))) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 40, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("0" = "#2563EB", "1" = "#DC2626"),
    labels = c("Control", "Treated"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "IPTW weight",
    y = "Density",
    title = sprintf("IPTW Weight Distribution (max=%.1f)", max(df$w_ate))
  )

# Effective sample size vs trimming threshold
trim_thresholds <- seq(0.05, 0.40, length.out = 30)
ess_vals <- vapply(trim_thresholds, function(t) {
  df_trim <- df[df$ps >= t & df$ps <= 1 - t, ]
  n <- nrow(df_trim)
  w_t <- df_trim$statin * 1 / pmin(pmax(df_trim$ps, t), 1 - t)
  (n^2) / ((sum(w_t)^2) / n)
}, numeric(1))
ess_df <- tibble(threshold = trim_thresholds, ess = ess_vals)

p_ess <- ggplot(ess_df, aes(threshold, ess)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#16A34A", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "PS trimming threshold",
    y = "Effective sample size",
    title = "Effective Sample Size vs Trimming"
  )

p_overlap <- p_ps + p_w + p_ess
print(p_overlap)
```

## 4. Placebo Outcome & Refutation Tests


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Test 1: Placebo outcome — an outcome that should NOT be affected by treatment
# Eye color should not be caused by statin use!
set.seed(5)
df$eye_color <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.35)  # purely random

placebo_mod <- glm(
  as.formula(paste("eye_color ~ statin +", paste(COVARIATES, collapse = " + "))),
  data = df, family = binomial()
)
placebo_or <- exp(unname(coef(placebo_mod)[["statin"]]))
cat("Placebo outcome test (eye color ~ statin):\n")
```

```{.r .cell-code}
# Test 2: Random treatment permutation — break any true causal effect
set.seed(42)
permutation_ors <- numeric(200)
placebo_form <- as.formula(paste("mi ~ statin_perm +", paste(COVARIATES, collapse = " + ")))
for (i in seq_len(200)) {
  df_perm <- df
  df_perm$statin_perm <- sample(df$statin)
  lr_perm <- glm(placebo_form, data = df_perm, family = binomial())
  permutation_ors[i] <- exp(unname(coef(lr_perm)[["statin_perm"]]))
}

perm_or_null <- permutation_ors
p_perm <- mean(perm_or_null <= adj_or)

cat("Permutation refutation test:\n")
```

## 5. Clinical Reporting Template


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Build a comprehensive causal inference report
placebo_status <- if (placebo_or > 0.85 && placebo_or < 1.15)
  sprintf("Eye color OR=%.3f (PASS)", placebo_or) else "FAIL"

report <- list(
  `Study question`    = "Effect of statin use on 30-day MI risk",
  Design              = "Observational cohort with propensity score adjustment",
  N                   = N,
  Treatment           = sprintf("Statin use: %.1f%%", mean(statin) * 100),
  Outcome             = sprintf("MI: %.1f%%", mean(mi) * 100),
  Identification      = "Backdoor adjustment (Age, Smoking, CHD history, LDL, SES)",
  Estimator           = "Adjusted logistic regression + G-computation",
  `Point estimate OR` = round(adj_or, 3),
  `E-value`           = round(ev, 2),
  `Common support`    = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_support),
  `Placebo test`      = placebo_status,
  `Permutation test`  = sprintf("p=%.4f", p_perm)
)

cat(paste(rep("=", 60), collapse = ""), "\n")
```

1. E-value = 2.1 for your statin analysis. Is this large or small? What known confounders (e.g. healthy user bias) have RRs in this range?
2. Your PS distribution shows poor overlap for elderly patients (age >80). What are your options?

5. Calculate Rosenbaum's gamma (how much unmeasured confounding would change the conclusion) using a simple sign test.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Exercise 5 — simplified Rosenbaum gamma bound
# For a binary outcome, test how much gamma (odds of differential unmeasured confounding)
# would be needed to make the result non-significant

# Use matched pairs analysis (simplified)
# In matched pairs, under gamma=1 (no hidden bias), we expect binomial with p=0.5
set.seed(42)
# Find pseudo-matched pairs (PS matching)
simple_match <- function(df, ps_col = "ps", treatment = "statin") {
  treated <- df[df[[treatment]] == 1, ]
  control <- df[df[[treatment]] == 0, ]
  treated <- treated[order(treated[[ps_col]]), ]
  control <- control[order(control[[ps_col]]), ]
  n_pairs <- min(nrow(treated), nrow(control))
  list(
    y_t = treated$mi[seq_len(n_pairs)],
    y_c = control$mi[seq_len(n_pairs)]
  )
}

pairs <- simple_match(df)
y_t <- pairs$y_t
y_c <- pairs$y_c
# Discordant pairs (pairs where outcome differs)
disc <- y_t != y_c
n_disc <- sum(disc)
n_treated_wins <- sum((y_t < y_c) & disc)  # treated has LOWER MI rate
cat(sprintf("Discordant pairs: %d | Treated outcome better: %d\n",
            n_disc, n_treated_wins))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Discordant pairs: 80 | Treated outcome better: 40
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Under gamma=1: test statistic ~ Binomial(n_disc, 0.5)
p_gamma1 <- pbinom(n_treated_wins, n_disc, 0.5)  # one-sided
cat(sprintf("p-value at gamma=1 (no hidden bias): %.6f\n", p_gamma1))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Find gamma that makes p = 0.05
p_at_gamma <- function(gamma) {
  p_plus <- gamma / (1 + gamma)
  pbinom(n_treated_wins, n_disc, p_plus) - 0.05
}

gamma_threshold <- tryCatch(
  uniroot(p_at_gamma, interval = c(1, 10))$root,
  error = function(e) NA_real_
)
if (!is.na(gamma_threshold)) {
  cat(sprintf("Gamma threshold (Rosenbaum): %.2f\n", gamma_threshold))
  cat(sprintf("  Unmeasured confounding must change treatment odds by >%.2f-fold\n",
              gamma_threshold))
  cat("  to make the result non-significant at alpha=0.05\n")
} else {
  cat("Result is robust to extreme levels of unmeasured confounding (gamma > 10)\n")
}
```
